cues.title: The Goblin Who Talked
cues.subtitle: Campaign 1: The Lantern Road  -  Level 1  -  4 Emberfall 1047 AK
cues.text: Morning comes grey over Brindle Cross. Last night Lantern Thirty-Seven on the south road went dark, and goblins came up out of the night. Four strangers held the square together: a dwarf soldier, an elf archivist, a halfling card player and the shrine's young priestess. One goblin was taken alive. He has spent the night tied to a rain barrel outside the Crooked Kettle, and he has not said a word.
Brindle Cross  -  The Night Watch Ends  -  Morning
Dawn at the Crooked Kettle. Brannoc has not slept. The goblin tied to the rain barrel has not either.
Four shutters broken. Two arrows in the door. One goblin. Still one goblin.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Four shutters! And who's going to pay for those, the Eight? Him?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: He's got no purse. I checked. Twice.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Did you sit out here all night with that? There's a bed upstairs, you stubborn dwarf. I aired it myself.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: Somebody had to watch him.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Oriel comes across the square from the shrine with a loaf under one arm and a bowl held in both hands.
Morning, Mistress Fenn. Brannoc. Have either of you eaten? No. I can see you haven't.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Is that shrine bread? For a goblin? And what does Father Tobin say about that?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: He packed it.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Oriel holds out the bowl. The goblin looks at it, then at the dwarf, and does not move.
Well. Shout if he bites.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: Brindle Cross  -  Bread and a Name  -  Morning
Is this breakfast or an interrogation? I can't do both before noon.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: It is both, Mistress Mossfoot. I have prepared seven questions, in order of importance.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: One question. Who sent you. Then I stop being patient.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Brannoc. Stand behind me, please. Just stand. You're very good at standing.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Oriel kneels in the dirt so her eyes are level with the goblin's. Behind her, Brannoc folds his arms and becomes a wall.
I'm Oriel. That bread is yours, whatever you say. What's your name? Your real one.
cues.speaker: oriel

roll.purpose: c1: Get a hostile, half-starved goblin captive to talk by kneeling with bread and asking his name, while Brannoc stands

cues.text: The goblin looks at the bread, then at the wall behind her. Then he eats, fast, as if someone might take it back.
Rusk. Name is Rusk.
cues.speaker: rusk

cues.text: Thank you, Rusk. Why do goblins come down to our road at night?
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Shiny stones. From the tall lights. Goblins carry them up into the hills. To the boss.
cues.speaker: rusk

cues.text: Boss gives food. Sacks of meal. Boss gets the food from somewhere else. Rusk not asks. Asking gets you hit.
cues.speaker: rusk

cues.text: And what's one of those stones worth to a goblin, roughly?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Supper.
cues.speaker: rusk

cues.text: A lantern-core holds a living mote of divine flame. And someone is paying for them in porridge.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Ilsevel studies the goblin's face the way she studies a damaged page: slowly, and without blinking.

roll.purpose: c2: Read whether the goblin is telling the truth or only what keeps him fed. Ilsevel has studied goblins in books, never

cues.text: He is telling the truth. Look at his hands. He is not afraid of us. He is afraid of going back.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: No sending Rusk back. Please. Boss counts the goblins who come home with no stones.
cues.speaker: rusk

cues.text: Nobody's sending you anywhere today, Rusk. Eat.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: He's still tied up.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: He can be tied up and fed. Those aren't opposites.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Brindle Cross  -  The Velvet Thread  -  Day
By the well, Ilsevel writes up the morning. Tamsin reads over her shoulder, which Ilsevel has asked her twice not to do.
You've spelled goblin wrong, Professor. There's a second B.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: There is not. I have read four bestiaries, including Orrin's Lesser Folk of the Vael, 1019 edition. Not one has a second B.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Then four books are wrong. Happens to the best of us.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Ilsevel's eyes drop to Tamsin's wrist. A thin velvet thread is tied there, worn soft with age.
That thread. Velvet, knotted twice. You touch it whenever someone looks at you for too long.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: This? Lucky charm. My grandmother tied it on when I was small. Kept me out of trouble ever since.
cues.speaker: tamsin

roll.purpose: c3: Tamsin tells the grandmother story about the velvet thread; Ilsevel, who trusts records over people, listens for the: tamsin
c3: Tamsin tells the grandmother story about the velvet thread; Ilsevel, who trusts records over people, listens for the: ilsevel

cues.text: It is a good story, and well told. Ilsevel listens to all of it and believes none of it.
I do not believe a word of that. Technically, you have been in trouble since the moment I met you.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Ooh, look. There's your second B. Right there. Look closer.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Ilsevel does not look at the page. She writes one more line in the margin. Tamsin pretends not to see it.
Brindle Cross  -  Free Board  -  Day
Right. All four of you, here, where I can see you. Is that goblin in my cellar fed?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: Fed, and he has a blanket. He's asleep on your onions.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: On my onions. Of course he is.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: In fairness, Mistress Fenn, they're very comfortable onions. I tried them first.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: That south road is how flour, letters and doctors get to us. And not a soul in Brindle Cross knows how to light a lantern.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: So. Free board and hot meals at the Kettle, for as long as it takes, to whoever brings that light back.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: I'll go! I know the south road better than anyone. I've walked it a hundred times!
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: No.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: But I can...
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: No, lad. Somebody stays and holds the village. That's you.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: I will go. Inspecting those lanterns is the task the Order gave me, and the ledger for Thirty-Seven is wrong. I intend to know why.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: I'll go too. It's my road. I felt that light go out. Someone should be there when it comes back.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Free board, you said? Free is my favourite word, Mistress Fenn. Count me in.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Nobody asks why a card player would want to walk an empty road out of town. Brannoc looks as if he might.
And you, soldier? Haven't you got letters to carry?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: Letters can wait. Road's dark. Somebody has to hold it.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Big Man, was that a speech? I think that was a speech.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Ten words. Don't get used to it.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Next time: The long walk to Lantern Thirty-Seven.
